questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing and blinking a lot
Yawning often or rubbing your eyes

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, confused thoughts, forgetting what you just drove, missing exits or signs, trouble holding your head up, drifting out of your lane, following too close, hitting shoulder rumble strips, or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice in a row
Always be done in the same order
Not be done if you know the vehicle well

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order
questions.explanation: Do your vehicle inspection in the same order every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes it less likely you will miss something.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Back up quickly to get out of other drivers' way
Try not to use your mirrors
Use a helper, if you can

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper, if you can
questions.explanation: Backing up a large truck is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper when possible.

questions.question: What does Gross Combination Weight mean?

options.text: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo together
The total weight of one vehicle without any load
The highest weight the manufacturer allows

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo together
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight (GCW) is the combined weight of the truck, all trailers, and the cargo being carried.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that slows your vehicle and reduces braking wear. But it can cause wheels to skid on wet, snowy, or icy roads. Turn off the retarder in these conditions.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors, you should:

options.text: Stare at the mirror for a long time
Use only the driver's side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the mirror quickly
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors quickly. If you look too long at a mirror, you may travel a long distance without seeing what is ahead of you.

questions.question: When passengers have carry-on bags, the best way to store them is to:

options.text: Lean them against the rear exit door
Leave them near the front door
Secure them so all exit doors are easy to reach

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so all exit doors are easy to reach
questions.explanation: Do not allow luggage in the aisle or doorway. All bags must be stored so passengers can quickly exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, you should:

options.text: Use the right turn signal, then the left turn signal
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights
Swerve side to side to get their attention

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells drivers behind you that you are slowing down. Always communicate your actions to other drivers.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you in a large vehicle, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Increase the space between you and the car ahead
Let the other vehicle pass you

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, slow down gradually and leave more space ahead. This lets the tailgater pass safely. Do not speed up—the tailgater will just follow at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: Emergency equipment like fire extinguishers is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials
Required in all commercial motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Required in all commercial motor vehicles
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry proper emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Back up in a straight line.
Wait until you are very far off course before correcting drift.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to safely turn left. Always start your left turn in the rightmost turn lane.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, how should you do it?

options.text: Keep the engine running and the vehicle in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Use a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: To check your vehicle's lights, turn off the engine, set the parking brake, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and flashers. Get out of the vehicle and look at each light to make sure it works.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hitting a hazard on the road?

options.text: Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Swerving to avoid a hazard is sometimes safer than stopping. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: What is the only way to become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up—not coffee, cold showers, or exercise. The only way to sober up is to wait.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on a commercial vehicle?

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashlight.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have spare fuses, warning triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: After starting an engine, what should warning lights and buzzers do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off right away.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging systems, and ABS should turn off immediately.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always inspect your vehicle before driving.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: They drive at a steady speed.
They stop without a clear reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop without a clear reason.
questions.explanation: Signs of an impaired driver include trouble staying in a lane, inconsistent speed, or stopping without reason.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is most like:
questions.correctAnswerText: Water skiing.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is like water skiing. Your tires slide on a layer of water and lose grip with the road.
